headline: Clinical Systems Implementation Lead | EMR Rollout and Adoption | MBBS-Trained Physician
summary: Clinical implementation lead with four years at Greenway Health taking EHR implementations from discovery through setup, training and adoption for close to 200 client practices. Trained 200+ providers, nurse practitioners, nurses and medical assistants, and treated adoption issues as product intelligence, turning them into features the product team shipped. Patient Safety Committee member who triaged issues through stage-gate release. MBBS-trained physician who understands clinical teams' workflows from the inside.
greenway_bullets: Owned end-to-end EHR implementations for close to 200 client practices, from discovery and workflow documentation through configuration, setup and adoption.
Ran discovery with each practice to document pain points, business processes and goals, then designed and configured practice-specific workflows and widgets.
Trained 200+ end users, including providers, nurse practitioners, nurses and medical assistants, on the new workflows.
Turned recurring client pain points into feature requests and worked with product teams to get them built; many shipped to clients.
Triaged defects and patient safety issues from detection through stage-gate release as a member of the Patient Safety and Functional Advisory Committees.
Clinical lead for a new AI-first EHR from Aug 2025: defined provider personas, mapped end-to-end clinical workflows and built React prototypes before engineering handoff.
Presented to clients and at the Greenway Engage provider conference.
skills: business discovery, requirements gathering, current- and future-state workflow mapping, system configuration, go-live and setup support, go-live readiness, post-implementation review
role-based end-user training, clinical staff training, SOP writing, user adoption, stakeholder communication
defect triage, patient safety review, stage-gate release, clinical documentation workflows, emergency, ICU and inpatient care
thesis_html: Adoption issues are product intelligence. I've treated them that way for four years.
why_fit: 200+ users trained across clinical and admin roles.
Patient Safety Committee: defects triaged through stage-gate release.
